findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: docs/work/checklist/2026-08-21-1.29.0-arbitrary-embedding-models.json item 'source-path-anchor-resolves-its-chunk', and docs/work/checklist/2026-08-22-1.30.0-code-corpus.json items 'source-path-anchor-resolves-its-chunk' and finding entry #2
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: Both runs reproduced and traced a real defect: 'a re-ingested file leaves its previous chunks behind' — direct memory_ingest_file of the same source path a second time (with different content) left the OLD chunk rows in the entries table alongside the new ones, so search could return content no longer in the file. Traced to FileIngestor.InsertChunksAsync never running a delete-by-source-path step (unlike the watch/repair paths' ReplaceAsync). Both runs marked their 'source-path-anchor-resolves-its-chunk' item NOT accepted because of this, and the 1.30.0 run recorded it as tracked-but-deferred (PR declined for that cycle, 'stays open, flagged for owner routing O5').
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: FIXED on 1.31.0 (PR #420, credited in this branch's HEAD commit history — 'chore(release): VERSION 1.31.0 — re-ingest prune, sync HMAC, activation pins, hardening wave'). Live-verified twice in this run: (1) re-ingesting direct/sextant.md after growing it from 1 chunk to 4 chunks left NO trace of the old single-chunk row (hash 6db4461154) — only the new 4 chunks remained; (2) a dedicated fixture (direct/sextant.md shrunk from 4 chunks to 1 completely different chunk, with direct/companion.md ingested as an untouched sibling control) showed all 4 old chunk hashes (08c559ad4f/62e06a8087/5e0198b8ba/8ea5ad89a9) gone from entries, exactly 1 new chunk (1d2c27123c) present, the sibling's chunk (f3027c9ad4) byte-identical/untouched, and a search for the old content's distinctive vocabulary ('micrometer drum perpendicularity index mirror side error') returned zero hits from sextant.md.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: sqlite3 ?mode=ro entries table before/after re-ingest (see item 'direct-reingest-prunes-stale-chunks' below for the full command/evidence trail); src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Ingestion/FileIngestor.cs now includes the delete-then-insert step this run traced (not re-diagnosed here, per the task's own instruction — confirmed by behavior, not by re-reading the diff).
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: This run's own item 6 (source-path-anchor-resolves-its-chunk) can now be ACCEPTED where both prior runs withheld acceptance — the '#section is not a query syntax' substitution still stands (unchanged product behavior, correctly identified by both prior runs), but the defect that blocked acceptance is gone. items.evidence:
ingest -> {"scanned":2} (calculator.cs + notes.md; bin/ and secret_config.md excluded).
settings table: EMPTY (no embedding.* rows at all — confirms zero model configuration).
entries: notes.md, embed_state='pending', embedding=NULL. code_entries: calculator.cs, embed_state='pending', embedding=NULL.

items.observed-result: CORRECTION to the item's own wording: the memory doc is NOT actually embedded out-of-the-box — embed_state stays 'pending' with a NULL embedding blob, exactly like the code corpus, until a provider is explicitly configured via 'model set local' or 'model set code local'. This matches ADR-0063's actual, narrower scope ('an unset provider resolves to the bundled engine' for CHUNKING/token-counting purposes only, not for activating real embedding) and the 1.30.0 run's own note that 'ai-raccoon model set local is NOT run automatically on a fresh bank.' The item's expected-result phrase 'embeds the memory docs (bundled model)' overstates what 'bundled model' resolution actually does (chunk-budget/tokenizer selection, not embedding activation) — this is a checklist wording imprecision, not a product defect, and is recorded here rather than silently reworded.

items.expected-result: memory_ingest_file of a file (N chunks), then modifying it so it chunks to a different count and re-ingesting: the superseded chunks are GONE (search no longer returns removed content; chunk set matches the new content exactly). Negative control: a sibling ingested file's chunks are untouched.
items.command: memory_ingest_file direct/sextant.md (4 chunks: 08c559ad4f/62e06a8087/5e0198b8ba/8ea5ad89a9) ; memory_ingest_file direct/companion.md (1 chunk: f3027c9ad4, sibling control) ; overwrote sextant.md with unrelated 1-chunk content ; memory_ingest_file direct/sextant.md again ; sqlite3 ?mode=ro entries for both source files ; memory_search for the old sextant vocabulary
items.evidence:
Before: sextant.md 4 rows (chunk_index 0-3/4). companion.md 1 row.
After re-ingest: sextant.md exactly 1 row (hash 1d2c27123c, new content) — all 4 old hashes GONE. companion.md STILL exactly 1 row, SAME hash (f3027c9ad4), byte-identical, untouched.
memory_search 'micrometer drum perpendicularity index mirror side error' -> 0 of the returned hashes are any of the 4 old sextant chunk hashes; the new sextant chunk (1d2c27123c) and companion.md both appear, ranked on their OWN (unrelated) content only.
items.observed-result: The direct memory_ingest_file path now prunes superseded chunks on re-ingest of the same source path, exactly like the watch/repair paths already did. A sibling file's chunks are provably untouched (identical hash, not just unchanged count).
items.acceptance-reason: Both the pruning and the negative control (sibling untouched by hash identity, not just row count) verified live. This directly contradicts and supersedes the 'not accepted' verdicts both 2026-08-21 and 2026-08-22-1.30.0 recorded for this defect — see findings-against-prior-runs.

items.expected-result: Tampering a model file AFTER its manifest was generated (flip one byte) makes model set refuse at activation, naming the sha256 pin mismatch; restoring the byte activates cleanly.
items.command: Hand-authored ai-raccoon.manifest.json (wordpiece, 384-dim, mean pooling, last_hidden_state output — matching the bundled model's real shape) around real copies of the bundled model.onnx + vocab.txt, with real sha256 of those exact files ; model set local <dir> (baseline) ; flip 1 byte in model.onnx at offset 1000 ; model set local <dir> again ; restore the byte ; model set local <dir> a third time
items.evidence:
baseline -> 'embedding engine set to local (.../shapin/model); re-embedding in the background' (exit 0).
tamper -> shasum changes 4278...02474 -> d1e3...ba11c. model set local -> exit 15: "Manifest '...' pins 'model.onnx' to sha256 4278...02474, but the file on disk hashes to d1e3...ba11c. The model directory may have been tampered with or partially replaced — re-run 'ai-raccoon model download' to restore a clean copy."
restore -> shasum back to 4278...02474. model set local -> 'embedding engine set to local (...); re-embedding in the background' (exit 0) again.
items.observed-result: Real sha256 pins over real, working model files: tampering causes an actionable refusal naming the exact expected-vs-actual hash, and restoring the byte returns to clean activation.
items.acceptance-reason: Used real sha256 pins over real, functioning bundled model files (not synthetic placeholder hashes), so both the refusal and the restore-to-success leg are proven against a model that genuinely activates, closing the gap a placeholder-hash fixture would leave.

items.expected-result: CLI command against a nonexistent bank exits 22 (NoBank); a settings-channel server error exits 23 (SettingsServerError), distinct from usage-error exits. Drive 23 live if a failing server can be arranged cheaply (e.g. point at a dead port); otherwise substituted naming the exit-code test class.
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <truly-nonexistent-dir> doctor ; echo $? ; (first attempt) a settings command against a --data-root with no server and default port 7721 accidentally dialed — corrected by using 'doctor' (CLI-local, no server needed) for the NoBank leg ; dotnet test --filter SettingsChannelExitCodeTests
items.evidence:
doctor against nonexistent bank -> 'ai-raccoon: doctor: no bank at .../memory.db'; echo $? -> 22.
Early probe of a settings command against an unreachable data-root's default port 7721 (before correcting to --port-aware doctor) returned exit 18 (SettingsServerUnavailable), NOT 23 — confirms per source (ExitCode.cs, ServerSettingsStore.cs) that a dead/unreachable port produces SettingsServerUnavailableException (18), not SettingsServerErrorException (23); 23 requires an actual 5xx HTTP response FROM a running settings server, which 'point at a dead port' cannot produce.
dotnet test --filter SettingsChannelExitCodeTests -> Passed! 2/2.
items.observed-result: NoBank(22) verified live via 'doctor' against a genuinely nonexistent bank path. SettingsServerError(23) requires a live server that answers with a 5xx, which cannot be arranged cheaply (a dead port produces the DIFFERENT SettingsServerUnavailable=18, live-confirmed here) — substituted per the item's own fallback.
items.acceptance-reason: 22 accepted as a live pass. 23 substituted, naming tests/AiRaccoon.Tests/Unit/Setup/SettingsChannelExitCodeTests.cs (2/2 passed on this build) — the item's own suggested live method ('point at a dead port') was tried and shown to produce exit 18, a different and also-real code, not 23; recorded here as a correction to the item's suggested method for future runs, not a finding against a prior checklist run.
